correctness.rationale: For every 0<p,q<1, max(0,p+q-1)<=r<=min(p,q), T>0 and x in [0,1], the empty-cycle probability h=1-p-q+r satisfies 0<=h<1. The conditional next-event recurrence V=(1-x)+(1-p)x+hV has the unique finite solution V=(1-px)/(p+q-r). On phase (0,x), the forward wait is x-t+(1-q)V; on phase (x,1), it is 1-t+(1-p)x+hV. Integration gives W/T=[2pq*x^2-2r*x+2-p-q+r]/[2(p+q-r)], whose strictly positive second derivative 2pq/(p+q-r) yields unique optimum min(1,r/(2pq)) including endpoints. The example p=q=r=2/5 gives optimal x=1 and exact waits 7T/5 versus 8T/5. The included verifier independently reproduces the result using rational forward recurrences, global-grid checks and supplementary random squared-headway simulations; finite checks are not the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader transit control and waiting-time frameworks do not supply the claimed phase law under arbitrary binary within-cycle dependence. The independent-departure result cannot imply a correlated two-opportunity case because its hypotheses exclude both two opportunities and non-independent outcomes; generic renewal-reward identities require evaluating the different point process.

originality.rationale: The inspected mathematical and transport literature addresses deterministic and stochastic headway costs, trip-time uncertainty, behavioral arrival patterns, and paired-route bus bunching, but not the exact labeled-cycle Bernoulli cancellation law with arbitrary within-cycle joint probability r, its covariance-dependent optimal phase and boundary regime r>=2pq. The fundamental residual waiting/renewal-reward principle is standard and is not claimed as new. Originality is conditional on the cited inspected evidence and has residual historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not certified. The 2006 Zhao et al. full text was not accessed; only its publisher abstract was checked.

The result assumes a cycle-labeled joint survival law not determined by physical-time weather correlation; real-world dependence may vary as schedules shift.

value.rationale: The precise and motivated objective is mean wait to the next usable service in a common-line corridor under shared disruptions. When within-cycle trip survival is not independent, half-spacing of the two nominal trips need not minimize the average waiting time. The exact covariance-controlled continuous optimum and high-correlation coincidence boundary identify a structure hidden by marginal reliability alone: with p=q=r=2/5, changing just the offset from half a cycle to a full cycle saves exactly T/5 expected waiting. The result is not presented as a calibrated transit planning policy and does not extend without proof to temporally correlated weather, continuously distributed delays, or capacity constraints.
